sector_model: Advertising technology platform: P/E and FCF after reported capex and capitalized software, take rate, CTV mix, gross pass-through working capital, term loan; GAAP tax distortions, SBC and political cyclicality adjusted for.
thesis: Magnite (Nasdaq: MGNI), sell-side programmatic advertising platform (CTV, mobile, desktop). Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-04) read in relevant sections. Q3 revenue 204.2M (+14%), 9M revenue 561.4M (+10%) with CTV +21% in 9M; 9M NI 57.8M vs 21.6M; 9M GAAP pretax 74.9M, tax 17.1M; 9M Adjusted EBITDA 196.8M (+33%, non-GAAP). Cash 392.9M vs term loan principal 357.7M (net cash about 35M); convertible notes of 205.1M repaid in cash in March 2026; rate cut by 50bp on 2026-10-07. 9M OCF 168.8M vs 107.7M; 9M buybacks 55.6M. Close 24.78 (2026-11-20) x 143.559M shares = 3.56B = 19.7x TTM NI 180.8M (inflated by a Q4 2025 tax allowance release; 9M26 pretax 74.9M), TTM FCF 224.1M (6.3%, after capitalized software), 3.7x book (own arithmetic). Fell 13.9% over the prior five sessions (28.79 on 11-16 open to 24.78). Possible market view: a Google-dependent open-web ad intermediary facing buyer power, with political ad lift in 2026. Differing evidence: CTV growth, EBITDA expansion, cash flow and the Google antitrust remedy plus Magnite's own suit. Not a recommendation.
counterthesis: Stock-based compensation was 55.8M in 9M (about 25% of TTM FCF if annualized), and buybacks only offset it. Q3 and 9M revenue include political advertising, which will not recur in 2027. OCF depends on gross working capital (receivables 1.43B, payables 1.74B) and swings with collection timing. Open-web display competes with Google's ad exchange; remedy outcomes and the Google Action are uncertain. Buyer concentration (large agency holding companies, demand platforms) and the five-session fall of nearly 14% were not explained. TTM earnings exaggerate normal profit because of the Q4 2025 tax release. Peers (PubMatic, Trade Desk, Criteo) and history not compared.
invalidation: Invalidated by CTV growth falling below about 10%, take-rate or fee concessions to buyers, Adjusted EBITDA margin gains reversing, FCF falling well below NI for several quarters, or an adverse Google remedy ruling that leaves SSP economics unchanged.
